To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) dioxin alters the hepatic transcriptome by AHR-dependent mechanisms; (2) dioxin does not alter the renal transcriptome by Ahr-dependent mechanisms; and (3) Ahr genotype alters the renal transcriptome, suggesting the presence and basal activity of an AHR gene battery in kidney.
dioxins and AHR regulate a large number of liver genes, and that the AHR regulates a large number of kidney genes, both in a dioxin-dependent and dioxin-independent manner.

1) dioxin exposure alters gene expression in both liver and kidney; 2) the liver transcriptome changes much more in response to dioxin than the kidney; 3) dioxin-dependent gene expression is highly tissue specific; 4) the Ahr gene battery is tissue specific; and 5) Ahr genotype has a large effect in liver and kidney.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Ahr gene in the development of the mouse kidney.
the role of the aryl hydrocarbon (AHR) receptor in the development of the mammalian embryo.
the role of dioxin-like chemicals in cancer and other diseases and with the mechanisms of dioxin action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AHR is a transcription factor that mediats responses to dioxines and other planar aryl hydrocarbons in a tissue specific manner.
the AHR is an important transcriptional regulator in both the liver and kidney, but that the specific effects of AHR activity in these tissues are distinct.
the liver is a dioxin-sensitive organ and the kidney is dioxin-insensitive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AHR is a transcription factor that regulates gene transcription in a tissue-specific manner.
the AHR is an essential regulator of the transcriptome, and its effects are highly context dependent.

dioxin exposure has a profound effect on the liver transcriptome but not the kidney transcriptome in wild-type mice, and that Ahr-null mice have profound differences in their transcriptomes in both the liver and kidney, with the liver transcriptome being more affected than the kidney transcriptome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AHR is a key regulator of the transcriptome in liver and kidney.
the AHR has a profound effect on gene expression in liver and kidney and that this is independent of dioxin.
AHR activity is important in liver and kidney in a basal, dioxin-independent manner.
